title: Reading Comprehension Labeling
subtitle: Highlight the answer. Review it together.
description: A self-hosted Rust + React workspace for SQuAD v1/v2 datasets: mark answer spans, review agreement and optionally request model suggestions.
longDescription: A self-hosted Rust + React workspace for SQuAD v1/v2 datasets: mark answer spans, review agreement and optionally request model suggestions. Rewritten from the original Flask application in 2026, keeping annotation, review and export in one workspace.
features: Answer-span annotation and SQuAD v1/v2 import/export
Optional model suggestions and built-in login
results: 2026 Rust and React rewrite with import, annotation, review and export
why: My first job had a Chinese reading-comprehension service to feed, and it needed questions with their answers marked exactly in the passage. I did the labelling myself too, which is the quickest way to learn what a labelling tool gets wrong.
gains: For teams building extractive QA or RAG evaluation sets: answers are stored as exact character offsets, a model can draft the first pass, and disagreements show up in review rather than in the trained model's answers.
lessons: Small local models write shaky questions, sometimes in the wrong language or with off-topic answers, which is why every suggestion needs a human click.
Browsers count UTF-16 units while SQuAD and Python count characters; the old version stored browser offsets, which an emoji throws off.
The old front end could submit without selecting an answer, stored as 0; those rows now import as questions still waiting for one.
